subject: categorical endogenous variable and WLSMV estimator

messages.author: 186c1ca2ff63c1ae
messages.subject: categorical endogenous variable and WLSMV estimator
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to fit a model with nine variables (no latent), including three endogenous and six exogenous.

One of the endogenous variables is a categorical (DAISIE.estab.DCH) coded as a binary (1/0). Therefore I use the WLSMV estimator.

Regarding the exogenous variables: EGF.perherb and EGF.annherb are two dummies used to code a three-level categorical variable; GRIN.Eur and EGF.veg are also binary variables (yes/no coded as 1/0).

Without any constraint (model1 below), the model is not identified (0 degrees of freedom, too many free parameters to be estimated compared to the number of variables). Now, when I fix the variances of all exogenous and endogenous variables to 1 (model2 below), the model is identified. However, rather than fixing variances and covariances I wanted to specify meanstructure=false, so that the model does not estimate the intercepts of the variables. But this is obviously not compatible with the WLSMV estimator, since it is a "mean and variance-adjusted" WLS method.

The fit of the model is bad anyway, but this is another matter. Here, I would like to ask whether what I do is correct (which I suspect not). Then, my questions are:

1) Do I properly handle the categorical variables (endogenous and exogenous)? If not, what am I doing wrong or what am I missing here?
2) Do I need to use the ordered=c("...") argument to specify which variables are binary or ordinal, or is specifying WLSMV as an estimator sufficient (given that these variables are already specified as factors in my data frame)?
3) Is there no estimator other than WLSMV that I can use here? In other words, do I necessarily need to estimate the intercepts of the variables in this model?
4) Given that the WLSMV requires means and variances, what is going on when I fix variances to 1?
5) The use of WLSMV implies a "scaled.shifted" test, right? It would be unsuitable here to use another test? (e.g. the Bollen-Stine bootstrap approach)

Below I paste model1 and model2 and a summary of the output for each.

Thank you very much in advance for your help.

Best,
Noëlie

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: categorical endogenous variable and WLSMV estimator
parts:
On 05/12/2014 06:08 PM, Noëlie Maurel wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I would like to fit a model with nine variables (no latent), including
> three endogenous and six exogenous.
>
> One of the endogenous variables is a categorical (DAISIE.estab.DCH)
> coded as a binary (1/0). Therefore I use the WLSMV estimator.
>
> Regarding the exogenous variables: EGF.perherb and EGF.annherb are two
> dummies used to code a three-level categorical variable; GRIN.Eur and
> EGF.veg are also binary variables (yes/no coded as 1/0).
So far, so good.

> Without any constraint (model1 below), the model is not identified (0
> degrees of freedom

Hold on. If you have df=0, your model is just identified. You just have
a saturated model. There is nothing wrong with that. But you do not get
a goodness-of-fit test.

BUT, you should not use std.ov=TRUE. You don not want to 'standardize'
the dummy variables. If you must standardize variables, do this in your
data.frame before calling lavaan.

Also, have you declared the endogenous categorical as 'ordered' in your
data.frame? I don't think so, since I do not see any thresholds in your
output. You can also use the ordered= argument in the sem() function.
Please see:

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html

> However, rather than fixing variances and covariances I wanted to
> specify meanstructure=false
Nope. You need the thresholds.

> Then, my questions are:
>
> 1) Do I properly handle the categorical variables (endogenous and
> exogenous)?
No. See above. You need the ordered= argument.

> 2) Do I need to use the ordered=c("...") argument to specify which
> variables are binary or ordinal
Yes.
> 3) Is there no estimator other than WLSMV that I can use here?
Perhaps ULSMV, but that will not solve your problem.
> 4) Given that the WLSMV requires means and variances

WLSMV does not require means and variances. The 'MV' only refers to the
correction of the test statistic. It is (or was) a 'mean and variance
adjusted' correction.

> 5) The use of WLSMV implies a "scaled.shifted" test, right? It would be
> unsuitable here to use another test? (e.g. the Bollen-Stine bootstrap
> approach)

You can use estimator="DWLS", in combination with se="bootstrap" and
test="bootstrap". This will take a while, but it should work.

Yves.
